title: Actual exam question for Salesforce's Analytics-Con-301 exam
question:
An executive-level workbook leverages 37 of the 103 fields included in a data source. Performance for the workbook is noticeably slower than other workbooks on the same Tableau Server.
What should the consultant do to improve performance of this workbook while following best practice?
option_A: Split some visualizations on the dashboard into many smaller visualizations on the same dashboard.
option_B: Connect to the data source via a custom SQL query.
option_C: Use filters, hide unused fields, and aggregate values.

title: Actual exam question for Salesforce's Analytics-Con-301 exam
question:
A client has a dashboard that renders in less than 10 seconds. The client receives a request to add a new calculated field that will return TRUE if a Project contains any one of the values "Project 1" or "Project 2" and FALSE otherwise. After adding the function found below, the dashboard's render time increases to 14 seconds from 10 seconds.
[Project] = 'Project 1' OR [Project] = 'Project 2'
Which function should the consultant use to reduce the render time?

title: Actual exam question for Salesforce's Analytics-Con-301 exam
question:
A university has data on its undergraduate students and their majors by grade level (Freshman, Sophomore, Junior, Senior). The university is interested in visualizing the path students take as they change majors across grade levels.
Which visualization type should the consultant recommend?

title: Actual exam question for Salesforce's Analytics-Con-301 exam
question:
A client has a data source that stores a time stamp for each time a user interacts with a product feature. They visualize 3 years of data at the daily level. As adoption has grown over the last 6 months, the dashboard performance has steadily decreased, despite connecting via a data extract that is set to refresh every hour.
A Tableau consultant needs to improve performance of the dashboard with the least impact to the visualization.
Which option meets these requirements without additional cost?
option_A: Add extract filters to limit the number of product features visualized.
option_B: Invest in an extract, transform, load (ETL) tool to aggregate the data to a daily level.
option_C: Decrease the extract refresh to once a day.
option_D: Leverage Tableau Prep to aggregate the data to the daily product level.

title: Actual exam question for Salesforce's Analytics-Con-301 exam
question:
A consultant has a view using a table calculation to calculate percent of total Sales by Category. The consultant would like to filter out particular categories, but wants the percent of total calculation to remain steady even as they filter items in or out.
What should the consultant do to achieve the desired impact?
option_A: Filter Category by using a Context Filter instead of a Dimension Filter.
option_B: Filter Category by using a Data Source Filter instead of a Dimension Filter.
option_C: Create an aggregate expression, and then use that instead of the table calculation.
option_D: Create a FIXED Level of Detail (LOD) expression, and then use that instead of the table calculation.

Which Level of Detail (LOD) expression should a consultant recommend?

title: Actual exam question for Salesforce's Analytics-Con-301 exam
question:
A client wants to see the average number of orders per customer per month, broken down by region. The client has created the following calculated field:
Orders per Customer: {FIXED [Customer ID]: COUNTD([Order ID])}
The client then creates a line chart that plots AVG(Orders per Customer) over MONTH(Order Date) by Region. The numbers shown by this chart are far higher than the customer expects.
The client asks a consultant to rewrite the calculation so the result meets their expectation.
Which calculation should the consultant use?

title: Actual exam question for Salesforce's Analytics-Con-301 exam
question:
A consultant is designing a dashboard that will be consumed on desktops, tablets, and phones. The consultant needs to implement a dashboard design that provides the best user experience across all the platforms.
Which approach should the consultant take to achieve these results?
option_A: Build one dashboard and fix the size of the dashboard.
option_B: Build one dashboard for each type of device and fix the size of the layouts.
option_C: Build one dashboard that has desktop, tablet, and phone layouts, and fix the size of the layouts.
option_D: Build one dashboard and set the size to Automatic.

title: Actual exam question for Salesforce's Analytics-Con-301 exam
question:

What is the most performant approach to model the data for a live connection?
option_A: Joining the tables in Tableau Prep
